title: Your AI Agent Can Now Pay Invoices. Set These 4 Guardrails First
content:
Your AI agent can now pay your invoices.
Before you let it, set these FOUR guardrails.
Yesterday Stripe announced Stripe Treasury for agents.
It lets startups run financial operations with agents, including ChatGPT and Claude.
According to Stripe, agents can check balances, pay invoices, transfer funds between accounts, and convert currencies.
And Stripe says spending limits for agents are coming in the next few weeks.
Why does this matter?
Stripe says that in the second quarter of this year, sixty three percent of C corps formed through Stripe Atlas were solo founders.
One person, running a company, with agents doing the admin.
So money is the next thing agents will touch. Here is how to do it safely.
Guardrail ONE. Start with read only.
Let the agent check balances, failed payments and refunds, and send you a daily report.
Stripe's own example is a solo founder whose agent sends him exactly that report every morning.
Only after weeks of clean reports should it be allowed to act.
Guardrail TWO. A human approves every payment.
The agent prepares the payment. You press yes.
Stripe says businesses choose when money movement needs human approval. Turn that on.
Now, guardrail three is the one most teams skip.
Guardrail THREE. Give the least access possible.
Stripe lets you choose which accounts and data an agent can see.
If it only pays contractors, it does not need access to your main reserve account.
Guardrail FOUR. Set limits and review the log every week.
Say you cap it at a small amount per payment, and review every transaction it prepared each Friday.
If something looks strange, you catch it in days, not months.
Here's my take. The risk is not that agents touch money.
The risk is giving them full access on day one.
Read, approve, least access, limits. Start there.
